edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from volume 1 of the Complete Works of Lu Xun (1948 printing); written 15 September 1924, first published in Threads of Talk (語絲) and collected in Wild Grass (野草), 1927.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自《鲁迅全集》第一卷（1948 年印本）；作于 1924 年 9 月 15 日，初刊于《语丝》，收入《野草》（1927）。

basis.en: First published in 1924; the author died in 1936. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1924 年首次发表，作者卒于 1936 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: The first piece of Wild Grass, Lu Xun's book of prose poems: two date trees, a strange high sky, a small pink flower dreaming of spring, and insects that fly into a lamp. It is here as an example of how much stubbornness a plain sentence can carry; the famous opening, a date tree and then another tree that is also a date tree, sounds like a slip until you see the trees refusing to bend. Notice the end, where he pays his respects to the little green insects as heroes.
note.zh: 《野草》的第一篇：两株枣树，奇怪而高的天空，一朵梦见春天的小粉红花，还有扑向灯火的小飞虫。收在这里，是因为它显示了平常的句子能承载多少倔强；那个有名的开头，一株是枣树，还有一株也是枣树，乍看像是笔误，直到你看见那树不肯弯曲。留意结尾，他对着灯默默敬奠那些苍翠精致的英雄们。

excerpt.orig: 在我的後園，可以看見牆外有兩株樹，一株是棗樹，還有一株也是棗樹。
excerpt.en: From my back garden two trees can be seen beyond the wall. One is a date tree, and the other is also a date tree.
excerpt.zh: 在我的后园，可以看见墙外有两株树，一株是枣树，还有一株也是枣树。
